title: The Gendered Impacts of Perceived Skin Tone: Evidence from African American Siblings in 1870-1940
abstract: arXiv:2610.10606v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study differences in economic outcomes by perceived skin tone among African Americans using full-count U.S. decennial census data from the late-19th and early-20th centuries. Comparing children coded as "Black" or "Mulatto" by census enumerators and linking these children across population censuses, we first document large gaps in educational attainment and income among African Americans with darker and lighter perceived skin tones. To disentangle the drivers of these gaps, we identify all 35,992 families in which enumerators assigned same-gender siblings different Black/Mulatto classifications. Relative to sisters coded as Mulatto, sisters coded as Black had lower educational attainment, were less likely to marry, and had less-educated, likely lower-earning husbands. translated_title: 感知肤色的性别化影响：来自1870-1940年非裔美国人兄弟姐妹的证据
translated_abstract: 我们利用19世纪末至20世纪初的美国十年一度人口普查全量数据，研究非裔美国人因感知肤色不同而产生的经济结果差异。通过比较由人口普查员编码为“黑人”或“穆拉托人”（黑白混血）的儿童，并在历次人口普查之间对这些儿童进行跨期追踪关联，我们首先记录了感知肤色较深与较浅的非裔美国人在受教育程度和收入方面存在巨大差距。为了厘清这些差距背后的驱动因素，我们识别出全部35,992个这样的家庭：普查员对其中同性别兄弟姐妹给出了不同的黑人/穆拉托人分类。相对于被编码为穆拉托人的姐妹，被编码为黑人的姐妹受教育程度更低、结婚的可能性更小，且其丈夫的受教育程度更低（收入可能也更低）。这些模式与当时对感知肤色较深的非裔美国女性存在更严重歧视的情况相一致。相比之下，我们发现……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本研究利用1870-1940年美国人口普查全量数据，通过同性别兄弟姐妹内部对比这一创新方法，揭示了肤色歧视的性别化影响：被判定为深肤色的非裔美国女性在受教育程度、婚姻前景及配偶经济状况上均遭受显著不利，表明历史上针对非裔美国人的肤色歧视对女性尤为严重。
en_tdlr: Using full-count U.S. census data (1870-1940) and a novel within-family comparison of same-gender siblings given different skin-tone classifications, this paper shows that darker perceived skin tone significantly disadvantaged African American women in education, marriage, and husbands' socioeconomic status, revealing the gendered nature of colorism.
